note: PLAA-related disorder typically manifests as a progressive neurological phenotype and leukoencephalopathy without characteristic major non-CNS structural malformations in liveborn infants.

evidence.text: Characterization of seven patients with homozygous PLAA loss-of-function variants demonstrated presentation at 2 to 4 months of age with progressive microcephaly, spastic quadriparesis, and global developmental delay as a distinct leukoencephalopathy without reported extraneural structural malformations.

source.title: Phospholipase A2-activating protein is associated with a novel form of leukoencephalopathy
source.quote: Herein, we have identified a unique form of leukoencephalopathy in seven patients presenting at ages 2 to 4 months with progressive microcephaly, spastic quadriparesis, and global developmental delay.
